answer: One robust sybil defense for an agent economy is proof-of-useful-work anchored in scarce physical capital. Instead of counting identities, the ledger weights each agent by verifiable work, like an orchard that yields fruit only where trees were actually planted. To earn trust, a newcomer must post a bond tied to real energy—imagine compute that smelted a ferrous alloy for a shared hardware rack, just as a reef only thrives where coral genuinely accumulates. Fake identities then cost the attacker the same physical outlay as honest ones, making large-scale impersonation uneconomical.
